summary: 14-day analysis of CGM and AAPS telemetry demonstrates exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and low variability (CV 12.9%). Overnight fasting glucose is stable at 102-112 mg/dL. Meal bolus strategies and AAPS SMB/UAM automation effectively manage postprandial excursions, returning glucose to baseline within 4 hours. No structural changes to basal rates, carb ratios, ISF, or DIA are indicated.
strengths: Time-in-Range is 99.7% with zero recorded hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) over 14 days.
Overnight glucose remains remarkably flat and stable within target range (102-112 mg/dL average).
Glycemic variability is exceptionally low with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%.
Postprandial glucose returns cleanly to baseline within 4 hours across all recorded meal patterns.
issues: Weekend brunch exhibits a moderate 2-hour postprandial peak (up to 188 mg/dL) due to higher carbohydrate/fat load, though glucose safely returns to baseline by hour 4 without manual intervention.
Telemetry export returns null values for specific SMB activation conditions and Autosens state toggles, requiring visual verification in the AAPS user interface.
education: A stable overnight glucose curve without drift or corrections is the clearest indicator of accurately tuned basal rates.

Using e-carbs (extended carbs) in AAPS helps model delayed fat/protein digestion by adjusting expected carbohydrate impact over time, enabling safe automated SMB delivery without risking late hypoglycemia.
Maintaining a prebolus interval of 15-20 minutes allows rapid-acting insulin peak action to align better with carbohydrate absorption, reducing 2-hour postprandial glucose spikes.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice or automated profile adjustment.
Always consult your diabetes healthcare team before making changes to basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratios, or sensitivity factors.
Make any parameter changes one at a time, verify them over several days, and monitor blood glucose closely.

analysis_steps.findings: 1,345 valid CGM entries over 14 days representing 100.0% data coverage without gaps. 28 meal/carb entries and complete active AAPS profile present.
analysis_steps.evidence: Coverage percent: 100.0%, gap count: 0, raw entry count: 1,345.

analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding glycemic safety with zero hypoglycemia recorded and minimal time spent above 180 mg/dL.
Scheduled basal rates accurately match endogenous fasting needs across all time segments, maintaining stable overnight glucose between 102 and 112 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local hours (23:00-06:00) show mean glucose between 102.3 and 112.9 mg/dL without required loop corrections.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios across breakfast (10 g/U), brunch (11 g/U), and dinner (9 g/U) successfully return glucose to baseline within 4 hours. DIA of 5.5 hours aligns with rapid-acting insulin kinetics.
analysis_steps.evidence: 4-hour postprandial glucose changes average -2 to +7 mg/dL at breakfast, -11 to +1 mg/dL at brunch, and -9 to +3 mg/dL at dinner.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Isolated pure correction boluses without carbs are rare due to high TIR.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM features operate safely and effectively, providing effective postprandial control without insulin stacking or hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific activation toggle flags return null in telemetry export.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max_basal 2.4 U/h, max_iob 8.0 U) provide appropriate safety bounds relative to scheduled basals and bolus sizes.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour=2.4 U/h is ~2.3x max scheduled basal (1.05 U/h); max_iob_units=8.0 U is ~1.4x max meal bolus (5.8 U).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens enabled state flag returns null in export.

analysis_steps.findings: Prebolus timing (10-20 min) and upfront bolus split (60-70%) align well with meal absorption profiles.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast 20-min prebolus limits peak glucose to <170 mg/dL; dinner limits peak to <140 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: The declared weekend brunch e-carb entry (20 g over 120 min) accurately models delayed absorption in higher-fat meals, allowing UAM/SMB to manage late rise smoothly.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch glucose recovers to 111-115 mg/dL at 240 minutes post-meal without late hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: All profile and automation parameters are well-calibrated and operate in harmony. No parameter changes are recommended. User should perform routine visual checks of UI activation toggles.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, stable overnight baseline, safe postprandial recoveries.

recommendations.title: Verify AAPS Activation Toggles in User Interface
recommendations.description: Telemetry exports return null for specific activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, autosens_enabled). Confirm these settings in the AAPS app UI to ensure they match your intended configuration.

recommendations.title: Optional Prebolus Trial for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch reaches a peak of ~188 mg/dL at 2 hours before returning to baseline at 4 hours. Extending prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes may help blunt this peak if desired.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all current basal rates, carb ratios, sensitivity factors, targets, and DIA settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile delivers an exceptional 99.7% Time-in-Range with zero hypoglycemia and low variability (CV 12.9%). Overnight and postprandial glucose curves confirm accurate calibration.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Continue standard monitoring and perform visual verification of AAPS UI toggles.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Administer 70% immediate bolus 15-20 minutes before standard meals, allowing active AAPS SMB/UAM to manage remaining postprandial carbs. Use e-carbs for higher-fat meals to accurately model delayed digestion.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: This strategy yields stable 4-hour postprandial recoveries across all meal types without causing insulin stacking or hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether extending weekend brunch prebolus to 15 minutes reduces the 2-hour peak below 160 mg/dL.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain 20-minute prebolus and 70% immediate upfront bolus.
exceptions.rationale: Keeps postprandial glucose peaks under 170 mg/dL with complete 4-hour return to baseline.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 10-15 minute prebolus, 60% immediate upfront bolus, and 20 g e-carbs over 120 minutes starting 15 minutes post-meal.
exceptions.rationale: Effectively models delayed fat/protein absorption, enabling safe SMB delivery without late-phase lows.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review this analysis with your diabetes care team.
Step 2: Confirm that your current profile settings match your clinical targets.
Step 3: Open the AAPS app UI to visually verify SMB activation toggles and Autosens settings that returned null in telemetry export.
Step 4: Continue monitoring blood glucose and meal responses without making mandatory profile parameter changes.
